title: A Pilot Case Series on the Use of a Large Mushroom-Shaped Corneal Graft for the Surgical Management of Post-Penetrating Keratoplasty Ectasia and Endothelial Failure

license.statement: CC BY 4.0 (article <license>: 'Creative Commons Attribution (CC BY) license', link https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)

indication: Ectasia after a previous penetrating keratoplasty (AvK >= 48 D or irregular astigmatism >= 8 D) combined with late endothelial failure of that graft (CCT > 600 µm or corneal edema without rejection); primary PK for keratoconus in 13/15, post-traumatic leukoma 1, infectious keratitis 1; other prior ocular surgery, glaucoma, retinal disease, advanced cataract and active rejection excluded

groups.description: Manual two-piece mushroom-shaped PK (after Busin et al.): one donor cornea split with a microkeratome into a large anterior lamella (9.0-9.5 mm) and a posterior lamella (~250 µm, 7.5-8.5 mm, sized to the previous graft) placed into a 9.0-9.5 mm partial-thickness recipient trephination with a central full-thickness opening; anterior lamella sutured (10-0 nylon), air in the AC when needed; chloramphenicol/betamethasone 4x/day for 1 month, 2x/day months 2-3, then hydrocortisone 0.3% 2x/day; 15 consecutive eyes of 15 patients, 2022-2023, retrospective, single centre

exclusions.what: CCT at 1 month in the Results text ('corneal thickness at the pupil center ... at 1 month')
exclusions.reason: Text value only, not a table cell
Figure, not a table cell; medians/IQR are not admissible

exclusions.what: Tables 1 and 2 rows BCVA, ECD, KMIN, KMAX, AVK and other baseline characteristics

notes: Role control: single-arm retrospective case series of consecutive patients treated with a two-piece mushroom PK (a technique introduced by Busin et al., applied here to post-PK ectasia with endothelial failure); no comparator and no arm declared experimental relative to a standard. The article calls it a pilot series of a surgical technique, so a treated role could be argued.
The preoperative reference is the edematous failing previous PK graft; postoperative CCT is of the new two-piece graft.
CCT method recorded as 'unstated': Methods list three devices that can measure thickness at every visit without saying which gave CCT; Results call it 'corneal thickness at the pupil center'.

All sutures were removed within a year; Results state that topometric parameters and BCVA at 12 months were measured after suture removal (not stated for CCT). Data were collected at 1 year in all patients (Methods), so n = 15 at each table time is expected but not stated.
Table 2 CCT cells are rounded forms of the Results-text means; the table cells are cited. One mild stromal rejection episode at 8 months resolved with topical steroids.

series.baseline_label: Preoperative CCT of the operated eyes (Table 1 'Baseline characteristics', row 'CCT (µm)')
series.notes: Table 1 row CCT (preoperative) and Table 2 row CCT at 6 and 12 months; mean ± SD in µm; the article does not name the CCT device (Methods list specular microscopy (Tomey), Oculus corneal topography and AS-OCT Casia II at every visit); per-visit n not reported
